page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-96-lssd is a memory-optimized and storage-integrated server instance from the c4 family. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). The instance is equipped with 744 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 6167 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 16 drives. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities alongside top-tier memory and storage performance. While single-core stress-ng performance falls in the average category, multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. The instance excels in memory bandwidth, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching the top 10% tier. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the top 10% tier, reflecting the high throughput of the local NVMe storage and memory subsystem. For LLM inference, prompt processing for medium (7B) models achieves top-tier speeds, though text generation for large (70B) models drops to average levels.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-highmem-96-lssd offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive memory capacity coupled with high-speed local storage. The primary tradeoff lies in single-core compute performance and large-model text generation speeds, which do not match the top-tier levels of its multi-threaded and database capabilities. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing.
